outputs.exact_statement:
Let $k=\mathbb F_2(q,H_1,H_2)$, where $q,H_1,H_2$ are algebraically independent. There exist a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra $\Lambda$ and a finite-dimensional nonprojective left $\Lambda$-module $Z$ such that $$\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}^i_\Lambda(Z,Z)=0=\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}^i_\Lambda(Z,\Lambda)
 \qquad\text{for every integer }i\geq1.$$ The module $Z$ is Gorenstein-projective. The semisimple quotient is $\Lambda/\mathop{\mathrm{rad}}\Lambda\simeq k^8$, so the algebra is split with eight isomorphism classes of simple modules; also $\mathop{\mathrm{rad}}(\Lambda)^4\ne0$. These conclusions persist after every field extension of $k$.

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional symmetric algebra over a field $k$ of characteristic two, let $F$ be a finite $A$-bimodule projective on both sides, and let $X$ be a finite left $A$-module. Suppose $v\in\underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}}_{A}(X,FX)$. For each integer $a$, put $$H^a=\underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}}_{A}(X,X[a]),\qquad
 K^a=\underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}}_{A}(X,(FX)[a]),$$ and define $$\label{conv:delta}
 \delta^a:H^a\oplus H^a\longrightarrow K^a,
 \qquad (g,j)\longmapsto F(g)v+v[a]j.$$ Assume that $\delta^0$ is surjective with nonzero kernel and that $\delta^a$ is an isomorphism for every integer $a>0$.*


*Choose an actual map $v_0:X\to FX$ representing $v$ and an embedding $i:X\to Q$ into a finite projective $A$-module. Define $$\label{conv:finite-module}
 \Lambda=\begin{pmatrix}A&0\\F&A\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 Y=(FX\oplus Q)/\{(v_0(x),i(x)):x\in X\},\qquad
 Z=(X,Y,\iota),$$ where $\iota:FX\to Y$ is induced by the first summand and specifies the structure map of the left triangular module. Then $Z$ is a finite nonprojective Gorenstein-projective left $\Lambda$-module and $$\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}^a_\Lambda(Z,Z)=0=\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}^a_\Lambda(Z,\Lambda)
 \qquad\text{for every integer }a>0.$$

Let $R$ be a finite-dimensional algebra over a field of characteristic two. Let $P_\bullet$ be a totally acyclic complex of finite projective left $R$-modules, and let $Q_\bullet$ be an exact complex of finite projective left $R$-modules. Put $$C_j(P_\bullet)=\mathop{\mathrm{coker}}(d^P_{j+1}:P_{j+1}\to P_j),\qquad
 M=C_0(P_\bullet),\qquad N=C_0(Q_\bullet).$$ There are natural, composition-compatible identifications $$H^0\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_R^\bullet(P_\bullet,Q_\bullet)
       \simeq\underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}}_{R}(M,N).$$ Applying this identification to shifted complexes gives, for every integer $a$, $$\label{conv:shift-comparison}
 H^a\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_R^\bullet(P_\bullet,Q_\bullet)
 \simeq\underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}}_{R}(C_a(P_\bullet),N)
 \simeq\underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}}_{R}(M,C_{-a}(Q_\bullet)).$$ For every integer $a>0$, these groups are naturally $\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}_R^a(M,N)$.

The rules [alg:C-corners]–[alg:C-products] define an associative unital algebra of dimension ten. Its radical is the span of the eight non-idempotent basis vectors, and $$(\mathop{\mathrm{rad}}C)^5=0,\qquad utut=q(1+q)z\ne0.$$

The algebra $T$ is symmetric of dimension twenty. A symmetrizing trace is $$\lambda(a,\phi)=\phi(1),$$ and the trace-dual of each basis letter is its starred letter. Its radical $\mathfrak r$ is the span of all basis letters except $e,f$; it satisfies $\mathfrak r^6=0$ and $T/\mathfrak r\cong k\times k$.

The cochain $p$ has weight $-1$ and is a Hochschild cocycle. Its associated class evaluated on $s$ is nonzero in $\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}_T^3(s,s)$.*


*For any $H\in k^\times$, let $h=h_H$ be the automorphism of $T$ fixing $C$ and multiplying $L$ by $H$. On the radical basis define $$z_H(a)=
 \begin{cases}
 Hqa,&a\in\{u,v,t,E,X,Y,Z,U,V\},\\
 0,&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}$$ and extend linearly. For all $a,b\in\mathfrak r$ one has $$\sum_{w\in\mathcal B_{\mathfrak r}}
      p(a,b,h(w))w^*
  =a z_H(b)+z_H(ab)+z_H(a)h^{-1}(b),
\label{coc:boundary}$$ where $\mathcal B_{\mathfrak r}$ is the radical basis.

A projective resolution $R\to s$ over $C$ has terms $$R_0=Cf,\qquad R_i=Ce\quad(i\geq1),$$ and differentials given by right multiplication: $$\cdots\longrightarrow Ce
 \xrightarrow{\,\cdot\ell_1\,}Ce
 \xrightarrow{\,\cdot\ell_0\,}Ce
 \xrightarrow{\,\cdot u\,}Cf\longrightarrow s\longrightarrow0.$$ More precisely, $d_{i+2}$ is right multiplication by $\ell_i$ for every $i\geq0$. For every integer $i\geq0$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}_C^i(s,s)=
 \begin{cases}k&i=0,\\0&i>0,\end{cases}
 \qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}_C^i(s,C)=
 \begin{cases}s^{\mathrm r}&i=2,\\0&i\ne2.\end{cases}$$ The second identification is an identification of right $C$-modules.

For the algebra $T=C\ltimes DC$ and its left $f$-simple $s$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}_T^*(s,s)=k[\tau],\qquad |\tau|=3,$$ as a graded algebra, where $\tau=p(s)$ is the evaluation of the cocycle from Lemma 7.

The simple left $A$-module $X$ is nonprojective, and $$\bigoplus_{a\geq0}\underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}}_{A}(X,X[a])
 =k[\tau_1,\tau_2],\qquad |\tau_1|=|\tau_2|=3.$$ The multiplication is composition with shifts, and its positive-degree part agrees with the ordinary Ext algebra.

Let $P$ be the bimodule bar resolution of $T$ and let $p:P\to P[3]$ be the selected comparison map. Form the ordinary complex $$K=\operatorname{Cone}(p:P[-3]\to P)
       \otimes_{k}\operatorname{Cone}(p:P[-3]\to P).$$ Then $K$ has finite projective $R$-terms and is exact in degrees greater than zero. For every $N\geq1$, its cokernel $C_N=\mathop{\mathrm{coker}}(K_{N+1}\to K_N)$ is finite and side-projective. Consequently $\mathcal C=\langle K\rangle$ has a finite side-projective module representative. The same conclusions hold for the first two filtration levels of $K$.

For the finite side-projective bimodule $\mathcal C$ of Lemma 11, put $$W^a=\underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}}_{A}(X,(\mathcal C\otimes_A X)[a]).$$ For every integer $a$, $$W^a=\begin{cases}k,&a=0\text{ or }3,\\0,&a\notin\{0,3\}. \end{cases}$$ Moreover the projection to the top cell induces an isomorphism $$W^3\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^{-1}. \label{cone:top-projection}$$

For each $H\in k^\times$, there is a stable bimodule map $$f_H:U_H\longrightarrow\mathcal C[3]$$ whose composite with the top-cell projection $\mathcal C[3]\to A[-1]$ is represented by the bimodule map $\beta_H:U_H\to\Omega A\subset P_0\otimes P_0$ determined by $$\beta_H(1)=\left(\sum_w h(w)\otimes_I w^*\right)
 \otimes\left(\sum_w h(w)\otimes_I w^*\right),$$ where each sum is over the letter basis of $T$. Under the canonical identification $U_H\otimes_A X\simeq X$, its projection after evaluation sends $$1\longmapsto H^2(f^*\otimes f^*)
 \quad\text{in}\quad
 \Omega X=\mathop{\mathrm{rad}}(A)(f\otimes f)\subset A(f\otimes f).$$ This evaluated map is nonzero modulo maps factoring through projectives. In particular, $f_HX$ is nonzero in $\underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}}_{A}(X,\mathcal C X[3])$.
On the nonnegative resolutions, with $B_{-1}=0$, one has $$dB+Bd=D_b.$$
There are bimodule maps $G_i:Q_i\to P_{i-1}$ for all $i\geq0$ such that $$pB=dG+Gd.$$
Under $U_H\otimes_A X\simeq X$, the evaluated map $\beta_H X$ sends $1$ to $H^2(f^*\otimes f^*)$ in $\Omega X\subset A(f\otimes f)$. It does not factor through a projective $A$-module.
For $H\in\{H_1,H_2\}$, tensoring with $U_H=A_{h_H\otimes h_H}$, under its canonical identification on $X$, acts on the whole space $H^{3m}$ as multiplication by $H^{-m}$ for every integer $m\ge0$.
The algebra $\Lambda$ is noncommutative, satisfies $\Lambda/\mathop{\mathrm{rad}}\Lambda\simeq k^8$, and has $\mathop{\mathrm{rad}}(\Lambda)^4\ne0$.
For every field extension $K/k$, the algebra $\Lambda_K=K\otimes_k\Lambda$ and module $Z_K=K\otimes_kZ$ satisfy all conclusions of Theorem 1 over $K$.

purpose: An explicit counterexample to the Auslander-Reiten conjecture

coverage.checked_domain: All 1000 ordered basis triples for associativity; all ten basis vectors for both unit actions; all radical basis words through length five and the displayed fourth radical product, over F_2[q].
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent dense SymPy polynomial tensor contraction; homogeneous positive grading proves the radical bound, while sparse python-flint multiplication enumerates radical words.
